sections.h2: Who sends the Murfreesboro property tax bill?
sections.html:
The Rutherford County Property Assessor appraises every parcel and prints the notices, and the City of Murfreesboro's Finance and Tax department collects the city share. The county's own share is collected by the Rutherford County Trustee, so a Murfreesboro owner has two payees.

  • Assessor's office: 319 N. Maple Street, Suite 200, Murfreesboro, TN 37130, phone (615) 898-7750. Use it for billing questions and to correct a mailing address.
  • City Finance Department: City Hall, 111 W. Vine St., first floor, phone (615) 893-5210, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County Trustee: Historic Courthouse on the Public Square, phone (615) 898-7705.

Murfreesboro's property tax page explains that the city applies its rate to the county's assessed value, then the county mails the bills and the city collects its portion.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Murfreesboro for a seller?
sections.html:
Murfreesboro is the seat of Rutherford County and lies about 34 miles southeast of downtown Nashville, within the Nashville metro area of Middle Tennessee. The 2020 census counted 152,769 people, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 171,178, a 12.0% increase from the 2020 base.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $402,100, with $382,600 for Rutherford County.
  • Homes lived in by their owners: 52.4%.
  • Median household income: $80,108.
  • Median gross rent: $1,481.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 43.0%.

The city covers about 63 square miles of land and has roughly 2,429 residents per square mile. The mean commute is 26.7 minutes. With a median home value above $400,000, a seller should know the exact tax owed before setting a price.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 reappraisal mean for a Murfreesboro tax bill?
sections.html:
Rutherford County runs a state-required countywide reappraisal every four years. The last one was in 2022, and the Assessor's FAQ says the next came in 2026. Values hold steady between those years except for new construction, additions, demolition or corrections.

A higher appraisal does not automatically raise the tax. Under Tennessee's certified tax rate law, a city or county must hold public hearings before adopting a rate that collects more in total than the year before. The Assessor adds that the tax rate is the County Commission's decision, not the Assessor's. The county's FAQ also explains that a lender's appraisal can differ from the Assessor's mass-appraisal value because a lender looks at one house in more depth.

The city's guidance on the calculation is simple: take the appraised value, multiply by 25 percent for residential property, 30 percent for business personal property or 40 percent for commercial, divide by 100, and multiply by the rate. The Trustee's FAQ lists the 2025 county rate as $1.8762 per $100. Because 2026 was a reappraisal year, ask the Trustee or the city for the rate printed on your current bill rather than reusing an old figure.

sections.h2: When is Murfreesboro city property tax due?
sections.html:
The city's October 2026 notice says tax is payable from October 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 without interest. Beginning March 1, 2027, unpaid base tax picks up 1.5 percent per month or any part of a month.

The city accepts cash, check or card, but not bank counter checks or two-party checks, and it takes partial payments. The county bill follows its own schedule: the Trustee's FAQ says it is due on the first Monday of October and can be paid until the last day of February without interest, and offers no early payment discount.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Rutherford County valuation?
sections.html:
The first step is a phone call or visit to the Assessor at (615) 898-7750, where an appraiser reviews the property record with you. Errors in square footage or a listed defect are the usual topics at this informal stage.

If you still disagree, the next stop is a hearing before the Rutherford County Board of Equalization. Its appeals are normally held in June, with appointments starting the first week of May. The board's 2026 notice lists hearings starting July 7, 2026, at the Assessor's office, and that season has ended. The notice warns that skipping the county board makes the assessment final without further appeal.

After the county board, the State Board of Equalization is the next level. Its hearings begin before an administrative law judge, and an appellant must pay a state fee. The last step is a suit in Davidson County Chancery Court. Appeals do not delay the bill, so pay on time and request any refund afterward.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists in Murfreesboro?
sections.html:
The state provides relief for elderly homeowners age 65 and over, for disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. The city page says the relief program is offered by both the City of Murfreesboro and Rutherford County, so an eligible owner files with both to cover the city and county bills. The deadline is 35 days after the city's delinquency date.

The Trustee's relief page adds a few specifics for veterans' households. A surviving spouse must have been married to the veteran at death and must not have remarried, and the property must be the applicant's primary residence. The page says the most market value used in the relief calculation is the first $175,000. Apply at the Trustee, (615) 898-7705, or the city tax office, (615) 893-5210.

Murfreesboro and Rutherford County have also approved the constitutional tax freeze for owners 65 and older. Contact the Trustee for forms. State relief does not erase the bill, and the Comptroller notes that it only reimburses taxes already paid.

sections.h2: How do you settle Murfreesboro property tax when you sell?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ tells a new owner to read the closing statement or ask the title company who pays the year's tax, and states that unpaid tax continues to accrue against the property. Check both city and county balances rather than only one, since the Murfreesboro portion is billed separately from the county's.

Delinquent real property tax can be paid online through the Rutherford County Chancery Court's online services, which list delinquent amounts. A seller with an old balance should ask the Chancery Court clerk for a current payoff figure, because costs and interest change it.

When the house is vacant or inherited and the bill is overdue, the practical sequence is to confirm the amounts owed, tell the title company about each office, and have them paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When is Murfreesboro city property tax due for 2026?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027 is the last day without interest. Bills were mailed and online payment opened October 1, 2026, and from March 1, 2027 interest runs at 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Who do I call with a question about my Murfreesboro tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Rutherford County Assessor at (615) 898-7750 for billing and address changes, and the City Tax Department at (615) 893-5210 for payments and relief programs.

faqs.q: Did Murfreesboro property values change in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. 2026 was a countywide reappraisal year in Rutherford County, with the prior one in 2022. Under the certified rate rules, higher values do not necessarily mean a higher bill, so check the rate on your notice.

faqs.q: Can seniors get a break on Murfreesboro property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state's relief program covers qualifying owners 65 and older, disabled owners and disabled veterans, and Murfreesboro and Rutherford County also approved a tax freeze for owners 65 and over.

faqs.q: How do I pay Murfreesboro property tax online?
faqs.a: Use murfreesborotntax.com with a card or e-check. The processor adds about 2.5 percent plus $0.30 for cards or $1.50 for an e-check. The county portion is paid separately through the Trustee.
